Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

strange adjective

odd, surprising, hard to explain

also odd, weird, peculiar, that’s strange, how odd, strangely, oddly enough, strange to say

classical

Ter. Haut. 1: Nē cui sit vestrum mīrum, cūr partēs senī …
Traupman 61: Mīrum est, that’s strange; Traupman 353, 386

mīrus, mīra, mīrum

adjective; mīrum est with an accusative and infinitive, quod, or an indirect question

strange, surprising, wonderful

What makes one wonder, for good or ill: mīrum est, that’s strange; mīrum in modum, strangely, amazingly; mīrum nī, “I’d be surprised if not”, so “surely”. It is also “wonderful” (see wonderful), and nec mīrum is “no wonder” (see be surprised).

Other words

  • īnsolitus, īnsolita, īnsolitum — unusual, unaccustomed, odd

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.361 (Lewis & Short): īnsolita mihi loquācitās; Traupman 353: īnsolitus, odd

    Strange because not usual: of a thing, uncommon; of a person, unused to something (īnsolitus ad labōrem, Caes. BC 3.85, Lewis & Short).

  • novus, nova, novum — new, unheard of, strange

    adjective · also used · classical

    Besides “new”, of what is novel and so unusual or strange: novum et mōribus veterum īnsolitum, a strange thing, unknown to the ways of the ancients (Tac. A. 12.37, Lewis & Short; see new).

Examples

  • Nē cui sit vestrum mīrum, cūr partēs senī poēta dederit quae sunt adolēscentium, id prīmum dīcam

    In case any of you thinks it strange that the poet has given an old man a young man’s part, I’ll explain that firstTer. Haut. 1–3

  • Mīrum nī domī est.

    He must be at home (it would be strange if he weren’t).Ter. And. 598

  • Mīrum est, nam valētūdine bonā ūteris.

    That’s strange, since you’re in good health.Traupman 61

  • Rīdiculum!

    How odd!Traupman 353

  • mīrābile dictū

    strange to sayTraupman 386

See also strange, be surprised, wonderful, new.
